newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower after Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower after Iraq news.

text.p: Swiss shares ended weaker on Tuesday but above session lows.
Prices were hit early in the day by fears of higher inflation, linked to worries that oil prices will rise in the wake of U.S. cruise missile attacks on Iraqi air defence targets.
Strong U.S. economic data released Tuesday added to the negative sentiment, with markets nervous before U.S. August jobs numbers on Friday.
Blue chips fell across the board with the exception of Swiss quality control concern Surveillance, which rose 20 francs to 2,820.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) lost 30.8 points, or 0.84 percent, to end at 3,623.9.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) retreated 18.59 points, or 0.79 percent, to 2,327.78 points.

Financial stocks were hit harder than industrials. UBS bearer shares, which led the actives list, shed 1.8 percent, or 21 francs, to 1,147. Other major Swiss banks and insurers were mostly over one percent lower.
Pharmaceuticals Ciba and Sandoz posted smaller losses. Roche certificaters yielded around one percent to 9,055 francs.
Nestle registereds shares were down eight francs to 1,399.

Second-tier hearing aid producer Phonak advanced six francs to 1,243 after the company proposed a dividend of seven francs for the 1995/96 business year, up from four francs paid out in the previous year.
